newsitem.title: UK: Ldn precious metals ignore news, stick to ranges.
newsitem.headline: Ldn precious metals ignore news, stick to ranges.

text.p: The precious metals on Monday shrugged off a slew of potentially bearish weekend news reports to hover in tiny ranges in European trading.
The gold market was barely lower, ignoring a U.S. Federal Reserve study arguing the United States and other governments should sell gold reserves to benefit their economies.

"It's a damning report, but the market's reaction has been zero. Gold has come off maybe $0.70 though the natural reaction should be bearish," a dealer said. Gold was fixed at $340.95 an ounce, versus Friday afternoon's fixing of $341.40.
The market may be simply dulled ahead of the summer slowdown, and many players are away from the market attending the Financial Times annual gold conference in Prague, dealers said.
The impact of the study, which is not to be seen reflecting the views of the Fed's board, may also be lessened by months of extensive debate on European central bank gold reserves.
The platinum group metals (PGMs) were also quiet, although the market was still very tight due to long delays from key producer Russia and a suspected squeeze by U.S. funds, dealers said.
Dealers said they were puzzling over a visit to Japan last week by officials of U.S.-based hedge fund Tiger Management.

The fund is believed to hold a vast amount of palladium through speculative trade, and traders in Tokyo who met the officials said the fund had tried to persuade them into buying palladium on a long-term basis. It was not clear whether any trade houses signed contracts to buy supplies from the fund.

But an analyst at the FT conference said the Tiger fund would have to take advantage of the situation quickly before Russian exports resumed or the opportunity will be greatly diminished as the price comes off.
Dealers in London said the situation could be explosive.

"It looks almost like brinkmanship. If the Japanese don't buy from the Tiger fund, it has to decide whether to stay long despite the Russians supplying the market, or decide it's a good profit," a dealer said. "You could see prices come crashing down or you could see the Tiger fund battling it out."
Platinum was quoted at $433.00/438.00, down $4, and palladium was $1.00 firmer at $203.00/208.00.
"There is short term lending in palladium in small amounts. But most people seem to be staying relatively square," he said.
Silver, was quoted just a cent lower at $4.71/4.73 an ounce.
